scenes.title: Bank scams
scenes.caption: How to spot a fake call from your bank.
scenes.say: Your bank has warned about a phone scam. Here's how it works, and what to do about it.

scenes.title: The call
scenes.caption: Criminals pretend to be the bank's fraud team.
scenes.say: Someone rings, or texts, or emails, saying they're from your bank's fraud team. The number on your phone may even look right.

scenes.title: The trick
scenes.caption: They say your money is at risk.
scenes.say: They say your account is in danger, and you must move your money to a safe account straight away. They may know your name and address.

scenes.title: Never
scenes.caption: Your bank will never ask for these things.
scenes.say: Your bank will never ask you to move money to a safe account. Nor for your full PIN, your password, or a code from a text.

scenes.title: Hang up
scenes.caption: Hang up. Do not trust the number on screen.
scenes.say: If a call like this comes, just hang up. Don't trust the number on your screen.

scenes.title: Call the bank
scenes.caption: Wait five minutes, then use the number on your card.
scenes.say: Wait five minutes, or use a different phone. Then call the number on the back of your card. If money has gone, call at once, or ring 159.

scenes.title: Take your time
scenes.caption: A real bank never rushes you. It's fine to say no.
scenes.say: Remember, a real bank will never rush you. Take your time. It's perfectly fine to say no.

scene 4: ticks beside things the bank never asks for read as 'yes, it asks'; crosses are needed
